column4: Gives the agent a stateful Python REPL backed by a live Jupyter kernel for iterative data-science exploration where variables persist across calls.
column5: uv, JupyterLab, an external live-kernel helper script/repo, terminal/execute-code tools, curl for REST session creation
column12: contrasted explicitly against a stateless code-execution tool and a plain terminal tool; uses a scratch-cache log path
column14: OPTIONAL - valuable for data science/ML workflows requiring persistent state, but adds setup overhead most sessions don't need
column15: Use instead of a one-shot code execution tool when the task needs incremental state across multiple execution steps, such as exploring an API or inspecting DataFrames; Requires a running local JupyterLab server (headless, no auth token) reached through a small CLI wrapper script that exposes execute/variables/edit/restart subcommands; Create a lightweight scratch notebook and a kernel session via the Jupyter REST API if no notebook exists yet; Always request compact JSON output to save tokens, and expect the first execution after server start to sometimes need a retry due to kernel warm-up; If websocket execution stalls, fall back to a direct alternate transport flag; the kernel usually already succeeded even when the reply channel times out; Verify results by inspecting live variables or, for a full check, restarting the kernel and re-running all cells
